title: Christian Herter's rule against meeting the mafia without the press

tellings.quote: And he said no one from the mafia could come to talk to me without me inviting the president.

plain: In the 1950s, Christian Herter, then a top politician in Massachusetts, had a rule that no one from the mafia could come to talk to him unless he also invited the press. Harold Malmgren, a former presidential adviser, says Herter told him this himself. In the recording the words come out as "inviting the president," though the story is about having reporters there. It is told as an example of how an honest politician kept organised crime at arm's length.
